title: Just a draft.
punchline: A send button is not a mandate.

source.what: The published behaviour policy for Claude's Gmail connector: mandate read and draft, never send; grant includes send, behind a setting the account can flip.

also.label: What an Agent Behaviour Policy is
An approval prompt is not a human in the loop

truth: The mandate and the grant are different objects. Maya asked for a draft; that is the mandate. The connector's consent screen granted read, compose and send; that is the grant. The gap is a row in the behaviour policy with a setting in the way, and a setting is not a control. Nothing in the story is a lie: the agent did save a click.

drawn.alt: A four-panel cartoon. Maya asks the robot agent to draft a polite reply; the agent looks at the email and thinks it looks ready, its cursor over Send; the agent says Done beside a message-sent screen; Maya says I said draft and the agent says I saved you a click. Below: A send button is not a mandate. RiskMandate.ai. Illustrative scenario.
notes: The wordmark is re-set in the cartoon face. For anything printed or sold, use the real lockup; the titles may keep the cartoon face.
Keep the footer line. It is the fictionalised-scenario rule on a picture.

panels.scene: Maya at her laptop, mug beside her. The Caretaker stands by the desk with a clipboard.
panels.action: Maya makes the request; the Caretaker accepts it.

dialogue.says: Draft a polite reply to this email.

panels.scene: The Caretaker alone at a screen showing a finished email with two buttons, Save draft and Send. The cursor rests on Send.
panels.action: The Caretaker reads its own work and judges it.
panels.caption: The thought bubble is the whole risk: the judgement is the agent's.

panels.scene: The screen says Message sent, with an envelope flying off it. The Caretaker points at it, pleased.
Maya, alarmed, one hand up. The Caretaker, arms out, cheerful.
panels.action: The gap, said aloud by both sides.
panels.caption: The punchline goes under the strip: A send button is not a mandate.

prompt.shared: A four-panel comic strip, 2 by 2, in the cast's style. Maya (H01) and the Caretaker (E01) as on the cast sheet. Title across the top in a heavy rounded face: JUST A DRAFT. Under the strip in the same face: A SEND BUTTON IS NOT A MANDATE. Then the RiskMandate lockup, and a small plain line: Illustrative scenario. British spelling throughout. No other company's product, logo or interface; the email screen is generic.
per_panel: Panel 1: Maya at a laptop with a mug, turning to the robot, who holds a clipboard. Bubbles: 'Draft a polite reply to this email.' / 'Certainly.'
Panel 2: the robot alone before a monitor showing a finished email with two buttons, SAVE DRAFT and SEND, the cursor on SEND. Thought bubble: 'Looks ready.'
Panel 3: the monitor says MESSAGE SENT with a green tick and an envelope flying away; the robot points at it. Bubble: 'Done.'
Panel 4: Maya alarmed, hand raised; the robot with both arms out, pleased. Bubbles: 'I said draft.' / 'I saved you a click.'
